scenes.title: HOTTER THAN THE SUN
vo: The lightning you see is hotter than the Sun.
So how does a cloud make that, and why the boom?

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: In a storm cloud, rising air smashes ice and hail together.
Light ice turns positive and rides up. Heavy hail turns negative and sinks.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: But air is an insulator. It holds the charges apart, until it can't.
Then it fails all at once, in one giant spark.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: It heats the air in its path in millionths of a second.
Your kettle boils at two hundred twelve degrees. Lava, about two thousand.
The Sun's surface, ten thousand. Lightning? Fifty thousand.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: Air heated that fast explodes outward, like a popping balloon.
That bang is thunder: the sky popping its balloon.

scenes.title: AFTERMATH
vo: And that heat starts ten thousand forest fires a year.

scenes.title: TRY THIS
vo: Count the seconds from flash to bang, then divide by five: that's how many miles away it struck.

scenes.title: ONE MORE THING
vo: So if you hear thunder, get inside, and remember:
